as_written_in_papers.quote: p.Arg376Pro (c.1127G>C), which was previously reported as a pathologic variant in AxD [4].

cases.statement: One carrier: a 51-year-old Korean man (heterozygous) with adult-onset AxD and later vestibulopathy. Two brothers had suggestive symptoms but were not genetically tested.

people.label: patient
people.key_phenotypes: knee hyperreflexia; cervicomedullary atrophy and tadpole-like brainstem atrophy with eyespot signs on MRI; slowly progressive spastic gait; dysarthria and dizziness after head trauma; right vestibulopathy with macrosaccadic oscillations

quotes.quote: A 51-year-old man presented with abnormalities on cervical spine MRI after a minor car accident.
He did not have any neurological symptoms, but on neurological examination, hyperreflexia in the bilateral deep tendon reflex of the knees was observed.
Brain MRI revealed tadpole-like brainstem atrophy (Figure 1B) and eyespot signs in the corticospinal tract of the medulla (Figure 1C and D)
His gait was spastic, and the spasticity was slowly progressive.
He was diagnosed with right vestibulopathy and treated with betahistine.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Adult-onset AxD pattern (cervicomedullary and tadpole-like brainstem atrophy, spastic gait). The scope of the next-generation sequencing test and whether other genes or causes were excluded are not reported.

quotes.quote: Cervical spine MRI revealed a lateral medullary cleft and marked cervicomedullary atrophy with intramedullary signal changes (Figure 1A).
Next-generation sequencing revealed a pathogenic heterozygous missense mutation of the GFAP gene

segregation.statement: No relative was genetically tested. Older brother (intellectual disability and gait disturbance since childhood, died at 52) and younger brother (intellectual disability) are marked as suspicious relatives without genetic confirmation; parents and three sisters reported without similar symptoms.

quotes.quote: His older brother had exhibited mental retardation and gait disturbance since childhood and committed suicide at the age of 52.
His younger brother also exhibited mental retardation.
However, his parents and three sisters exhibited no similar symptoms
the dots indicate suspicious relatives (older and younger brothers) without genetic confirmation.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense, p.(Arg376Pro). The paper gives no variant-level mechanism statement; it describes AxD as caused by autosomal dominant or de novo GFAP mutations.

quotes.quote: Alexander dsease (AxD) is a progressive astrocytic leukodystrophy primarily attributed to autosomal dominant or de novo mutations in the GFAP gene [1].

authors_classification.statement: Called a pathogenic heterozygous missense mutation, previously reported as a pathologic variant in AxD (citing reference 4, Heshmatzad et al. 2022, PMID 36088400, not in the batch).

quotes.quote: Next-generation sequencing revealed a pathogenic heterozygous missense mutation of the GFAP gene, p.Arg376Pro (c.1127G>C), which was previously reported as a pathologic variant in AxD [4].

concerns: The authors cite an earlier report of the same variant (reference 4: Heshmatzad et al. 2022, Eur J Med Res, PMID 36088400, an Iranian family); that paper is not in the batch, so its carriers are not represented here.
No transcript is stated in the paper.
Two brothers with childhood-onset intellectual disability and gait disturbance were not genetically tested; whether they share the variant is unknown.
The paper does not describe the sequencing test's gene scope or any other variants found.
notes_for_panel: One person, adult onset, no relative tested. The prior report cited by the authors may hold more carriers.
